cards.identity: Transport every non-Clifford rotation backwards through the Clifford skeleton as a Pauli rotation and merge any two that share an axis, WITHOUT rebuilding the circuit. Write the op list as U = ... G_m ... where each non-Clifford op at position p is R_p = exp(-i a_p Z_{q_p} / 2) (rz(a_p), t = a_p=pi/4, tdg = a_p=-pi/4). For an ordered pair of rotation positions i < j: initialise P := Z_{q_j} (a signed Pauli string on all n qubits) and walk the ops strictly between j and i in REVERSE order. (a) For a Clifford op C on qubits Q, set P := C P C^dag (v3.api.pauli.conjugate(P, C, Q)); this is the backward transport, since C R = R' C with R' = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2). (b) For a rotation op at position k (i<k<j) on qubit q_k, require commutes_with_z(P, q_k) (P's letter on q_k is I or Z); if so R_k and the transported rotation commute and we may slide past, otherwise ABORT the pair. On arrival just after position i, require P = s * Z_{q_i} with s in {+1,-1} and identity letters elsewhere (is_z / exact Pauli equality, no numerics). If the test passes the match is (i, j, s) and apply() replaces the angle at i by a_i + s*a_j and DELETES position j; every other op, including the whole Clifford skeleton, is byte-identical. Matches are emitted for all passing pairs, greedily by increasing j and nearest admissible i, and the runner verifies each one. with_ops lowers a merged angle that lands on a multiple of pi/4 to Clifford/T automatically.
cards.correctness: Two facts, both exact at the level of signed Pauli strings (no floating point enters the decision). (1) Clifford conjugation: for any Clifford C and Pauli P, C exp(-i a P/2) = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2) C, because C f(P) C^dag = f(C P C^dag) for the analytic function f(x)=exp(-i a x/2) and C P C^dag is again a signed Pauli (Gottesman-Knill). Walking the Clifford ops between j and i in reverse therefore computes exactly the axis P such that the whole segment S (Cliffords only) satisfies S exp(-i a_j Z_{q_j}/2) = exp(-i a_j P/2) S. (2) Commuting Pauli rotations commute: if [P, Z_{q_k}] = 0 then exp(-i a P/2) and exp(-i a_k Z_{q_k}/2) commute (they are simultaneously diagonalisable), so the transported rotation passes the intervening rotation R_k unchanged; commutes_with_z(P,q_k) is exactly this symplectic test, since P and Z_{q_k} anticommute iff P's letter on q_k is X or Y. Combining, R_j can be moved to sit immediately after position i while every other op is unchanged. Arriving with P = s Z_{q_i} gives exp(-i a_i Z_{q_i}/2) exp(-i s a_j Z_{q_i}/2) = exp(-i (a_i + s a_j) Z_{q_i}/2), using exp(-i a P/2)exp(-i b P/2) = exp(-i(a+b)P/2) for a single axis and exp(-i a (-P)/2) = exp(+i a P/2) for s = -1. No global phase is introduced (all factors are special-unitary rotations), so the replacement is exact up to global phase. This strictly generalises the book's phase_polynomial_rotation_merge: that rule needs a Hadamard-free segment and compares affine Z-parity labels, which is the special case where every transported axis stays a pure Z-type string; here Hadamards, S and CZ are absorbed into the Pauli frame, so rotations separated by Hadamards (the dominant pattern on this circuit) can be merged, and the admissibility test is Pauli commutation rather than label equality.
cards.trigger: Any pair of rotation positions i < j in the op list (names rz/t/tdg, i.e. rotation(op) is not None) such that the reverse walk above yields P = +-Z_{q_i} and commutes_with_z(P, q_k) holds for every intervening rotation position k. Angles need NOT be equal or related: any a_i, a_j merge into a_i + s a_j, so the trigger is purely structural. The walk may cross h, s, sdg, x, z, cx, cz freely (x and z only flip the sign of P, which is tracked). Abort conditions: an intervening rotation whose qubit carries X or Y in P, or arrival with P not supported solely on q_i as a Z. On hhl_8: 785 rotation ops (583 rz + 101 t + 101 tdg) over 2208 ops, 8 qubits, with 607 Hadamards, so the overwhelming majority of candidate pairs are exactly the ones the Hadamard-free book rule cannot see ('h rz h' x117, 'h h rz' x96, 'rz h s' x92, 'sdg h rz' x58 in the trigram table).

The book rule already captured the Hadamard-free merges (35450 -> 34266, about 20 rotations). Lifting the merge test into the global Pauli frame should reach the merges that pyzx's phase-teleportation finds (pyzx: 29205, i.e. ~105 rotations removed from the TKET input), since phase teleportation is the ZX-calculus version of the same spider-fusion-under-Clifford-frame argument. Estimating ~65-75 further rz deletions beyond the book (the Pauli-frame test is more conservative than ZX graph-like reduction because it keeps the Clifford skeleton fixed and requires exact +-Z_{q_i} arrival), that is ~70*58 = 4060 T removed plus ~450 T from the relaxed per-rotation epsilon, with a handful of merged angles landing on multiples of pi/4 and collapsing to free Clifford/S gates. cards.name: rotation_count_minimal_block_refit
cards.identity: Numerical re-instantiation of small windows against an ansatz chosen to minimise the NUMBER of non-Clifford Z-rotations, not the gate count. (1) Partition the op list into blocks: scan left to right and grow a block greedily while its qubit support stays <= 3 and every op added is dependency-contiguous (an op may join only if no op outside the block separates it from the block on a shared wire); close the block when a 4th qubit would be needed. Record for each block B its qubit support S (|S| = 1, 2 or 3), its exact target unitary U_B = product of its ops (dense 2^|S| matrix, built with numpy from the op list; rz angles as given), its number of non-Clifford rotations r_B (ops with rotation(op) not None and angle not a multiple of pi/4) and its CX/CZ count c_B. (2) For each block with r_B >= 2, search for a shorter realisation: enumerate candidate ansaetze A(r, c) in lexicographic order of (r, c) for r = 0, 1, ..., r_B - 1 and c = 0, ..., c_B, where A(r, c) is a fixed template of c two-qubit Cliffords (CX/CZ on the pairs actually used inside B, in the order they occur in B) interleaved with single-qubit layers, each single-qubit layer being an Euler word rz(x) h rz(y) h rz(z) on each wire of S; the free parameters are all the rz angles, of which at most r are allowed to stay non-Clifford and the rest are CONSTRAINED to the Clifford+T grid (multiples of pi/4, enumerated over the 8 values, or solved for and then snapped). Instantiate the free angles by least-squares minimisation of the phase-invariant residual f(theta) = 1 - |tr(V(theta)^dag U_B)| / 2^|S| with scipy.optimize (L-BFGS-B / least_squares), from K = 30 deterministic restarts (fixed seed; include the block's own angles and the Euler angles of the KAK/ZXZ decomposition of U_B as starts). (3) Accept the first (r, c) whose best fit reaches phase-aligned operator distance d_B = || V(theta) - e^{i phi} U_B ||_2 <= 1e-10 with r < r_B and c <= c_B. (4) Post-snap: any fitted angle within 1e-10 of a multiple of pi/4 is emitted as the exact Clifford/T gate (with_ops does this), any angle within 1e-10 of 0 or 2pi is dropped; re-measure d_B after snapping. (5) The match is (block span, replacement op list); apply() splices the replacement in place of the block's ops, every op outside the block byte-identical. Emit matches for all blocks that compress, in block order; the runner verifies and costs each one separately. Degenerate case |S| = 1 is the classical Euler collapse: any maximal single-wire run, however many rz and h it contains, is realised by rz h rz h rz, i.e. at most 3 non-Clifford rotations.
cards.correctness: Three separate arguments. (a) The target is exact: U_B is the product of the block's own ops computed in dense linear algebra, so the specification of the local rewrite is exactly 'replace a unitary by another unitary on the same qubits'. Since the block is dependency-contiguous (no outside op interleaves on a shared wire), the global circuit factors as W_2 (U_B tensor I) W_1, and replacing U_B by V gives W_2 (V tensor I) W_1; by unitary invariance and submultiplicativity of the operator norm, || W_2 (V tensor I) W_1 - e^{i phi} W_2 (U_B tensor I) W_1 || = || V - e^{i phi} U_B || = d_B. So the global error contributed by the block is exactly its measured local distance, which is what the frozen judge charges to the budget; errors of different blocks add subadditively, total <= sum d_B. With d_B <= 1e-10 and at most a few hundred blocks the total charge is <= 1e-7, four orders of magnitude under the approx allowance eps/2 = 5e-4, so this rule consumes essentially none of the error budget and does not tighten eps_rz for the surviving rotations. (b) Completeness of the ansatz family: the Euler word rz(x) h rz(y) h rz(z) generates all of SU(2) up to global phase (ZXZ Euler angles, since h rz(y) h = rx(y)), and interleaving arbitrary single-qubit layers with the block's own CX/CZ pattern reproduces the block itself as one member of the family (take the block's own angles), so the search is a restriction, never an extension, of what the original block can express: for c = c_B and r = r_B the fit is exact by construction, and the enumeration simply asks whether a smaller r suffices. Hence an accepted fit is always a strict reduction in non-Clifford rotation count at no increase in two-qubit gate count. (c) Why slack exists at all on a TKET-FullPeepholeOptimise'd input: TKET's peephole optimises two-qubit blocks for CX count and total gate count under the KAK decomposition, and squashes single-qubit runs into a normal form with up to three rotations each; it does not minimise the number of rotations whose angle is NOT a multiple of pi/4, which is the only thing the gridsynth cost model charges for. A KAK Cartan vector with components that are multiples of pi/4 (exactly what QFT/QPE controlled-phase gates produce: the dyadic angles pi/8, pi/16, pi/32, 5pi/64 visible in the angle histogram arise from controlled-rz gates whose Cartan part is a single non-Clifford angle plus Clifford local terms) is emitted by TKET as three generic rotations; the (r, c) enumeration with the non-free angles pinned to the pi/4 grid finds the representation that keeps one non-Clifford angle and makes the other two Clifford. The judge re-verifies every single application, so a bad fit cannot be accepted: an accepted application is certified by the frozen verifier, not by the optimiser's residual.
cards.trigger: Any dependency-contiguous block of consecutive ops with qubit support of size <= 3 containing at least 2 non-Clifford rotations (angle not a multiple of pi/4), for which step (2)-(3) finds a fit with phase-aligned distance <= 1e-10, strictly fewer non-Clifford rotations and no more CX/CZ gates than the block. On hhl_8 the op list is 2208 ops on 8 qubits with 497 cx, 583 rz, 607 h, 175 s, 119 sdg, 101 t, 101 tdg: greedy <= 3-qubit blocks between the points where a 4th qubit enters give on the order of 150-250 blocks, and with 583 non-Clifford rotations the rotation-rich blocks (the trigram table shows the dominant local shapes 'h rz h' x117, 'rz cx rz' x79, 'rz h s' x92, 'h s cx' x92, 'sdg h rz' x58, i.e. rotations sandwiched between Cliffords on few wires) typically carry 3-8 non-Clifford rotations on 2-3 wires - far below the 15 (SU(4)) / 63 (SU(8)) parameters the ansatz family provides, so each such block is heavily over-parameterised and compresses. Blocks that do not compress simply emit no match. The rule is orthogonal to the two book rules: pauli_frame_rotation_merge and pauli_exponential_commutation_merge only ever DELETE a rotation whose transported axis equals +-Z on an earlier rotation's qubit and which commutes with every rotation in between (that pairwise test is necessary as well as sufficient for same-axis merging with a fixed Clifford skeleton, which is why they saturate at the pyzx phase-teleportation number 29205); this rule instead REBUILDS the Clifford skeleton of a block numerically and so removes rotations that no same-axis merge can ever reach.
cards.expected_effect: Every non-Clifford rotation removed saves one gridsynth sequence. At the current N_Rz the per-rotation cost is 3 log2(1/eps_rz) + O(log log) ~ 55-59 T, and because eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz, dropping rotations also loosens eps_rz for all survivors (about 0.8 T less per surviving rotation per 100 removed). Expected compression: single-wire runs give the Euler bound (<= 3 non-Clifford rotations per maximal run, worth a few tens of rotations); the bulk comes from 2-qubit and 3-qubit rotation-rich blocks, where the pi/4-pinned enumeration typically turns a 4-6 rotation block into a 2-3 rotation block, i.e. roughly a 35-45% cut in rotation count overall. From 583 rotations down to ~360-380 is ~210 rotations removed: ~210 x 57 = ~12000 T less, partly offset because the survivors' per-rotation count is only mildly cheaper and because some blocks will not compress at all (dependency-contiguous <= 3-qubit windows in a circuit with 497 CNOTs on 8 qubits are sometimes too narrow to contain 2 rotations). Netting that out against the measured ceiling of the best numerical-refit baseline on this circuit (BQSKit-DPF, 19443 T, which is exactly the regime a <= 3-qubit numerical re-instantiation pass reaches), I expect ~29205 -> ~21500-22000. CX count cannot regress (c <= c_B per block), qubit count is untouched (no ancillas), and the error charge is ~1e-7 total, so no lexicographic tie-breaker and no budget constraint is harmed.
cards.source: Numerical instantiation / block resynthesis as in BQSKit: Younis, Iancu, Lavrijsen, Davis, Smith, 'QFAST / Berkeley Quantum Synthesis Toolkit' and Smith, Davis, Younis et al., 'LEAP: Scaling numerical optimization-based synthesis using an incremental approach' (ACM TQC 2022); Patel, Younis, Iancu, de Jong, Mueller, 'QUEST: systematically approximating quantum circuits' (2022) for accepting fits under an explicit distance budget; KAK / Cartan two-qubit decomposition from Tucci and Vatan-Williams, 'Optimal quantum circuits for general two-qubit gates' (PRA 69, 032315); Ross and Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations' (arXiv:1403.2975) for the 3 log2(1/eps) cost model that makes rotation COUNT, not gate count, the objective.
